# In U.S., Millennials pass Gen X in debt, latest Equifax Global Credit Trends shows


October 21, 2026


A generational credit shift is underway, according to the[Equifax first half 2026 Global Credit Trends report](http://equifax.com/globalcredittrends) . **According to the latest report, Millennials in the U.S. now hold a larger share of debt than Gen X.** Also in the U.S., Gen Z is the fastest-growing credit group. Meanwhile, in the U.K., nearly 30% of Buy Now, Pay Later (BNPL) users aged 18 to 24 made no other traditional credit repayments.


The report, made possible by the[Equifax Cloud](https://www.equifax.com/about-equifax/equifax-cloud/) ™,[EFX.AI](http://efx.ai/) capabilities and the organization’s unique proprietary data, is designed to give lenders around the world a deeper view into overall consumer credit demand, debt, delinquencies, credit card utilization rates and inflation trends in their particular region to make more informed decisions and innovate faster – enabling more mainstream financial opportunities for consumers.


#### Millennials pass Gen X in the U.S.


In the first half of 2026, Millennials’ share of U.S. debt caught up with and passed that of Gen X. A surge in mortgage borrowing fueled the change as older generations paid down debt. Here is how each generation’s share of U.S. debt changed from January 2020 to May 2026:


-


**Millennials:** Up from 25.1% to 36.8%


-


**Gen X:** Down from 39.2% to 35.9%


-


**Baby Boomers:** Down from 30.3% to 20.1%


-


**Gen Z:** Up from 0.8% to 5.2%


-


**Traditionalists:** Down from 4.5% to 1.9%


Mortgages now make up 70% of Millennial debt, and 30% of Millennial borrowers hold one.


#### Gen Z is the fastest-growing credit group


Gen Z grew its share of U.S. debt from 4.8% in January 2026 to 5.2% in May 2026, making the segment the fastest-growing credit demographic. Partnering with these consumers as they build credit profiles is a prime opportunity for long-term growth and customer loyalty.


#### Young Canadians turn to family to buy homes


In Canada, high housing costs mean younger first-time buyers can rarely buy a home alone. **First-time buyers under 35 in Ontario and British Columbia are taking out joint mortgages with older borrowers, typically parents, at twice the rate of the rest of Canada.**


Homeowners in high-cost markets like Ontario also face pressures that outpace the rest of the country. Among Ontario mortgage holders, non-mortgage delinquency rose 27% year over year, compared with 2% in the rest of Canada.


#### BNPL reaches the next generation in the U.K.


BNPL is now entering regulation by the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA). Ahead of the change, the report uses proprietary transaction data to set a baseline. The data shows BNPL growing from an alternative payment method into core credit infrastructure.


-


**38%** of U.K. consumers used BNPL in 2025.


-


**45%** of users made five or more transactions in peak months.


-


**BNPL continues to gain** retail finance market share from credit cards, based on monthly repayment share.


BNPL is redefining financial inclusion, especially for the next generation of borrowers. **In 2025, 29% of BNPL users aged 18 to 24 made no other traditional credit repayments.** That compares with 16% of users aged 25 to 34 and 15% of all BNPL users.


**Explore the full 1H 2026 Global Credit Trends report at[equifax.com/globalcredittrends](http://equifax.com/globalcredittrends) .**
